PROSE:
Artie and Fizz managed to evade the shouting guards, ducking down a shadowed slope to slip through a rusted iron grate and descend into the damp gloom of the Oakhaven Crypts to test his new gear. The heavy iron grate slammed shut behind them, the metallic clang echoing down the stone tunnel and abruptly cutting off the enraged shouts of the Adventurer's Guild. 

Artie leaned against the cold, moss-slicked wall, his chest heaving as he tried to catch his breath. His cheap office suit clung to his sweaty pale skin, completely unsuited for fleeing through medieval alleyways, let alone exploring subterranean dungeons. 

`[Status Effect Removed: Safe Zone Active]`

The floating blue text hovered in Artie’s peripheral vision, a stark, terrifying reminder of his fragile mortality. He stared at the notification until it dissolved into digital sparks. In his old life, the most dangerous thing he faced was a papercut from a fresh ream of printer paper or the vending machine stealing his quarters. Now, the very concept of safety had been revoked by a glowing prompt.

He shivered, pulling the Cloak of the Cowardly Lion tighter around his shoulders. The garment was absurdly oversized, swallowing his skinny-fat frame entirely. It smelled faintly of mothballs, ozone, and synthetic fur, but Fizz had sworn it was exactly what he needed to survive his cursed stat allocation. He adjusted his grip on the Rusty Iron Dagger in his right hand, the metal cold, uncomfortably heavy, and offering absolutely zero reassurance.

"Are you absolutely certain this is a good idea?" Artie asked, his voice echoing slightly against the damp stone walls. He wiped a bead of sweat from his forehead, pushing his messy brown hair out of his eyes. "Because 'Safe Zone Active' just went away, and I am currently sitting at a grand total of one hit point."

`[HP: 1/1]`

Fizz floated lazily beside him, her neon-pink hair glowing like a tiny, pixelated beacon in the oppressive dark. Her digital-blue eyes blinked with an innocence that Artie was rapidly learning to distrust. "Relax, Artie! It’s a classic RPG exploit. High-level dungeon, high-tier loot, zero risk if you just don't get hit. The cloak provides a stealth modifier. You'll be practically invisible!"

"Practically invisible," Artie repeated, his tone flatter than a spreadsheet. He glanced down at himself. The Employee ID Badge still dangled from his neck lanyard, catching the dim light. The cursed Participation Trophy pinned to his lapel felt heavier than usual, radiating a faint, mocking warmth. "Right. And if I get sneezed on by a high-level mob, I explode into a shower of gore. I'm a glass cannon without the cannon part."

"Then don't get sneezed on," the AI chirped cheerfully, doing a small loop-the-loop in the air. "Just walk softly and let the stealth mechanics do the heavy lifting. The system rewards ingenuity!"

Artie let out a long, shaky breath. "Ingenuity. Right. Let's just hope the system doesn't reward ingenuity with a swift, brutal death." 

He crept deeper into the tunnel. The crypts were exactly what a mid-level accounting firm employee would imagine a dungeon to look like: dark, oppressive, and structurally unsound. Water dripped from the ceiling, pooling on the uneven cobblestones in stagnant puddles. The air grew colder with every step, carrying the unmistakable scent of ancient dust and dry rot. 

As they rounded a jagged corner, the narrow passage opened into a wide, ruined antechamber. Massive stone pillars, cracked and crumbling, held up a ceiling lost in the shadows. In the center of the room stood a towering skeletal guard. It was clad in rusted chainmail that hung off its ribcage like tattered rags, gripping a jagged iron sword that looked like it weighed more than Artie did.

`[Target: Skeletal Guard (Lvl. 8)]`

Artie froze, his back pressing so hard against the cold stone wall he felt the dampness seeping through his suit jacket. Level eight. He was level one, with exactly five experience points to his name. If that thing even looked at him too hard, the sheer force of its gaze would probably deplete his single hit point and send him back to the void.

"Okay," Artie whispered, barely moving his lips, his heart hammering against his ribs. "It's right there. What now?"

"Stealth time!" Fizz whispered back, hovering just behind his ear. "Just edge around the perimeter. Keep to the shadows. The cloak's enchantment will mask your presence. It’s basically a cheat code."

Artie nodded slowly, though he felt entirely unconvinced. He took a cautious step forward, carefully placing his dress shoe on the stone floor, rolling his weight from heel to toe just like he had seen in the movies. A soft, blue notification chimed in his vision.

`[Stealth: Active (Flawed)]`

Artie paused, his foot hovering an inch above the ground. He stared at the bracketed text. "*Flawed?* Fizz, what does 'Flawed' mean?"

"Oh, it's just a minor modifier," Fizz said, her voice entirely too breezy for the situation. She waved a tiny, translucent hand dismissively. "It means the item's stealth is highly effective, but it has a... thematic drawback."

"A thematic drawback," Artie hissed, his panic rising. He lowered his foot slowly. "What kind of thematic drawback? Fizz, this isn't a literature class!"

He didn't have to wait for an answer. As he shifted his weight to take his next step, the Cloak of the Cowardly Lion let out a loud, pathetic whimper. It wasn't Artie making the noise; the sound came directly from the synthetic fur draped over his shoulders, sounding exactly like a frightened dog realizing it was at the vet. 

The skeletal guard’s skull snapped up, the rusted chainmail clinking loudly in the silent room. 

Artie panicked, freezing in place like a deer in headlights. He tried to take a hasty step backward, desperately hoping the shadows would conceal him, but his heel came down hard on a pile of debris he hadn't noticed. Beneath the thick layer of crypt dust lay a brittle femur.

*CRACK.*

The sound was deafening in the echoing chamber, sharp as a gunshot. To make matters worse, the cloak let out another loud, cowardly yelp, trembling violently against his back and entirely ruining whatever stealth modifier it was supposed to provide. 

`[Stealth Check: Failed]`
`[Aggro Gained: Skeletal Guard]`

The heavy lion hood of the cloak slipped back, offering no concealment. Artie stands exposed as the skeleton turns its glowing eyes toward him, a bright red aggro marker pulsing violently above its skull.
